subject.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan

question: Should deep security audits adopt 1 MiB as the canonical installed-plugin manifest limit and accept warning-only fallback when declared extension entrypoints cannot be read?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but neither the threshold nor reduced declared-entry coverage for rejected manifests can be established as permanent security policy from tests or CI alone.

options.title: Approve the bounded audit policy
options.body: Keep the 1 MiB cap and warning-plus-directory-scan fallback as the intentional deep-audit security contract.

options.title: Align a shared manifest contract
options.body: Define or reuse one plugin-manifest size limit across audit and other manifest consumers before landing this patch.

options.title: Pause for stronger fallback coverage
options.body: Delay landing until rejected manifests receive a scan strategy that cannot miss normally skipped declared entrypoints.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded audit policy
recommendation.body: Keep the 1 MiB cap and warning-plus-directory-scan fallback as the intentional deep-audit security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated ownership of the fs-safe and TOCTOU security boundary used by this patch.
